# Workspace context

This file describes the machine and the workspace layout so that agents do not have to rediscover it or guess. Repository-specific instructions live in each repository's own `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` and take precedence for that repository. The statements below were checked on 2026-11-24; where a command is given, run it instead of trusting the statement.

## Environment

- A **Kubernetes pod**, not a laptop or a VM: a Coder workspace (`CODER` and `CODER_WORKSPACE_NAME` are set in the environment).
- The pod and its Coder template are managed from `mmalyska/home-ops` (GitOps: the template is in `cluster/apps/ai/coder/workspace-template-dev-workspace`, this workspace's RBAC in `cluster/apps/system/dev-workspace`). Changes to the pod itself (template, resources, mounts, RBAC) are made there, not on this machine. A template change reaches the pod only after `coder templates push dev-workspace` and `coder update <owner>/<workspace>`, which restarts the pod and ends running sessions. Both need the owner's consent.
- The image is `dev-workstation`, built from `mmalyska/containers` (`apps/dev-workstation`; its `mise.toml` lists every tool, apt only provides the OS). The pod keeps the image digest it started with, so a newer image reaches it only after a template update.
- Ubuntu, user `vscode` (uid 1000), no root and no sudo. The pod hostname looks like `ws-dev-workspace-<hash>` and changes when the pod is recreated.
- Tools are managed with `mise` (`mise ls`). To add one for your user: `mise use -g <tool>` (persists on the home volume); to add it for everyone, add it to the image's `mise.toml`. Dotfiles are managed with `chezmoi` from `mmalyska/dotfiles`. There is no TTY for prompts: `chezmoi update` stops on a changed managed file, so apply specific files instead (`chezmoi diff <path>`, then `chezmoi apply <path>`).
- Not installed on purpose (the image tests assert it): `sudo`, `gcc`, `cc`, `make`, `wget`, `nc`. `readelf` (binutils) is not installed either.
- Never print or commit `CODER_*` tokens or other credentials from the environment.

## Persistence

Two separate volumes (Ceph RBD, ext4) survive pod restarts:

- `/home/vscode` (about 5 GB): home directory, tool config, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, mise user installs, caches. It is small and was about 80 % full on 2026-11-24: run `df -h /home/vscode` before installing tools or downloading large files.
- `/workspaces` (about 30 GB): all git repositories.

Everything else on the filesystem (apt packages, `/usr/local`, `/tmp`, `/cache`) is lost when the pod is recreated; add it to the image or the mise config instead.

## What this workspace can and cannot do

This workspace is **read-only by design** (`home-ops`, `docs/src/k8s/dev-workspace.md`). Check any permission instead of assuming: `kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> [--subresource=exec]`, `kubectl auth can-i --list`.

- **Kubernetes:** `kubectl` uses the pod's service account `dev-workspace` (there is no kubeconfig and no current context). It can `get`, `list` and `watch` an explicit list of kinds (the ClusterRole `dev-workspace-reader`). It cannot read Secrets, `exec` into pods, or write anything: no cordon, drain, delete, patch or create. A read that is denied usually means the kind is not in the role. Adding it is a PR to `home-ops` (read the CRD's fields for inline credentials first; the method is in `docs/src/k8s/dev-workspace.md`, "CRD audit").
- **Talos:** `talosctl` has the role `os:reader`. `talosctl -n <node-ip> version` works; the Read API (`talosctl read /proc/...`) and any change, including a reboot, are denied.
- **In-cluster HTTP, reachable by service name:** Prometheus at `http://prometheus-stack-kube-prom-prometheus.monitoring.svc:9090`, Alertmanager at `http://prometheus-stack-kube-prom-alertmanager.monitoring.svc:9093`, Loki at `http://loki.monitoring.svc:3100`. No port-forward is needed. Loki keeps about 30 days, and a query over a longer range fails: split it. Creating or expiring an Alertmanager silence is a cluster change and needs the owner's consent.
- **GitHub:** `gh` and `git` over HTTPS use `GITHUB_TOKEN`, a fine-grained token: repositories, PRs and workflow dispatch work; the Packages API does not (HTTP 403). Public ghcr.io images can be read without a token: `curl "https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:<owner>/<image>:pull"` gives a pull token for `/v2/<owner>/<image>/tags/list`.
- **Argo CD:** the `argocd` CLI has a token in the environment; its permissions are in `docs/src/k8s/dev-workspace.md`. A sync changes the cluster and needs the owner's consent.
- **Always the owner's action, not this workspace's:** cordon, drain and reboot a node, `talosctl` changes, `exec` into a pod (for example the Ceph toolbox), Alertmanager silences, Argo CD syncs, deleting anything outside a git branch (ghcr packages, PVCs, secrets), `coder update`. Prepare the command and the checks, ask, then watch the result read-only.

## Secrets and credentials

- `BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `BWS_PROJECT_ID` come from the pod. The Bitwarden Secrets Manager project holds `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `TERRAFORM_TOKEN`, `ARGOCD_SERVER`, `ARGOCD_AUTH_TOKEN` and `SSH_SIGNING_KEY`.
- At pod start the Coder template exports every project secret except `SSH_SIGNING_KEY` as an environment variable to all processes, so they are already set in every shell, Claude and Codex session. They are read once: after rotating one in BWS the workspace must be restarted. Check with `[ -n "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]`; if one is missing, read it from BWS with `bws secret list "$BWS_PROJECT_ID"`. Never print values.
- `gh` uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` directly. `git` over HTTPS uses `gh auth git-credential` (set in `~/.gitconfig` by dotfiles). If a push hangs, the helper is missing: `chezmoi apply ~/.gitconfig`.
- Commits are SSH-signed with the key held in the in-pod ssh-agent (`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`); the private key is never in the environment or on disk.
- Never print, log or commit secret values. This file is public: it never holds a hostname, a token or a private repository name.

## Working conventions

- **Read a repository's instructions before anything else in it.** Only a session started inside a repository loads its `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`; a session started in `/workspaces` or in another repository does not. Before the first command that touches the repository, reads and greps included, read its `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`, else `README.md`) in full and follow it: for that repository it takes precedence over this file.
- Do repository changes in a **linked worktree**, not in the primary checkout, in every repository: `git worktree add .worktrees/<type>/<slug> -b <type>/<slug> origin/main`. A hook (the `git-workflows` plugin) blocks edits in a primary checkout. Keep each primary checkout on its default branch, clean, updated with `git pull --ff-only`, and remove a worktree and its branch after the PR is merged.
- The hook reads a command as text. If a command that only reads is denied while the shell is in a primary checkout, start it with `cd /tmp &&` or use absolute paths; creating a worktree and editing in it in one command can be denied too. The `git-workflows` plugin fixes both from version 1.3.12 on; check the installed version under `~/.claude/plugins`.
- Never push to the default branch; change repositories through PRs. Commits and PRs carry no AI attribution lines. **Push and open PRs only when the owner asks.** An action that changes the cluster or an outside service needs the owner's consent for that action.
- Don't modify cluster resources with `kubectl` directly if a repository manages them through GitOps; change the repository and let it reconcile.
- Start sessions inside the relevant repository, so this file and that repository's instructions are both loaded. A session started in `/workspaces` loads only this file and the global one, so the rule above applies.
